CL.name: Aromo australiano
CL.citation: Instituto Forestal de Chile (INFOR), technical bulletin 'Apuntes: Antecedentes Generales sobre Acacia melanoxylon (Aromo Australiano)' (revista.infor.cl): 'En Chile se le denomina principalmente aromo australiano.'

AR.name: Aromo salvaje
AR.citation: Same INFOR technical bulletin: 'Debido a su habilidad de invadir terrenos y bosques en Argentina recibe el nombre de aromo salvaje (Carnevale, 1968)'.

CO.name: Acacia negra de Tasmania
CO.citation: NaturaLista Colombia (iNaturalist Colombia national node), species page title 'acacia negra de Tasmania (Acacia melanoxylon)'; species confirmed present in Colombia per Kew POWO distribution data.

MX.name: Acacia de madera negra
MX.citation: CONABIO (Mexican federal biodiversity commission) SIVICOFF invasive-species technical fact sheet: 'Especie: Acacia melanoxylon, R.Br. Nombre comun: Acacia de madera negra.'

AU.name: Australian Blackwood
AU.citation: Wikipedia species article and Pl@ntNet World Flora record; the species is native to eastern Australia and Tasmania, where 'blackwood' is the standard timber-trade name (used for guitars, ukuleles, and other instruments as a substitute for koa wood).

GB.name: Blackwood
GB.citation: Same standard English timber-trade name; species distribution per Kew POWO explicitly includes Great Britain (naturalized).

US.name: Blackwood
US.citation: Same standard English name; species distribution includes California per Kew POWO/Colombian Plants aggregated distribution data, where it is documented as naturalized.
